extraction.name: XTREME-S
extraction.description: A benchmark to evaluate universal cross-lingual speech representations in many languages. It covers four task families: speech recognition, classification, speech-to-text translation and retrieval, covering 102 languages from 10+ language families and 3 different domains.
extraction.license: Permissive license that allows the use and redistribution of the data for research purposes
extraction.creator: Alexis Conneau, Ankur Bapna, Yu Zhang, Min Ma, Patrick von Platen, Anton Lozhkov, Colin Cherry, Ye Jia, Clara Rivera, Mihir Kale, Daan Van Esch, Vera Axelrod, Simran Khanuja, Jonathan H. Clark, Orhan Firat, Michael Auli, Sebastian Ruder, Jason Riesa, Melvin Johnson
extraction.publisher: Google Research, Hugging Face, Meta AI
extraction.citeAs: Conneau, A., Bapna, A., Zhang, Y., Ma, M., von Platen, P., Lozhkov, A., Cherry, C., Jia, Y., Rivera, C., Kale, M., Van Esch, D., Axelrod, V., Khanuja, S., Clark, J. H., Firat, O., Auli, M., Ruder, S., Riesa, J., & Johnson, M. (2022). XTREME-S: Evaluating Cross-lingual Speech Representations. arXiv:2203.10752v3.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: XTREME-S aggregates existing datasets (Fleurs, MLS, VoxPopuli, CoVoST-2, Minds-14). For the new Fleurs dataset, 2009 n-way parallel sentences from the FLoRes dev and devtest sets were used, and between one and three recordings were collected for each sentence in 102 languages.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: FLEURS is a dataset that is complete at more than 97%. Some slight improvements and changes may be done in a 2nd version of the dataset (e.g. missing recordings, or replaced low-quality recordings).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: FLoRes dev and devtest sets (for Fleurs), Librivox audiobooks (for MLS), European Parliament sessions (for VoxPopuli), read speech of Wikipedia and other sentences (for CommonVoice/CoVoST-2), e-banking domain spoken examples (for Minds-14).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For Minds-14, monolingual datasets were merged into a single multilingual dataset with a 30-20-50% train-dev-test split. For Fleurs, new train-dev-test splits were built with 1509, 150 and 350 sentences respectively.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Scripts are provided to download and easily reproduce the preprocessing steps. The XTREME-S HuggingFace Dataset tool provides the correct splits.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For Fleurs, between one and three recordings were collected for each sentence. For other datasets, existing annotations (transcriptions, translations, intents) were used.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Speakers of the train sets are different than speakers from the dev/test sets in Fleurs.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Updates will be made on the platform. Additional test sets may be added in the future to confirm the generalization ability of submissions.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Making speech technology available in all languages is especially important to give speakers of under-represented languages an equal voice on the Internet, and the possibility to make their content and culture known outside of their language cluster.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Results are much better on the Western European group than on other groups like Sub-Saharan African or South Asian, which can be explained in part due to the larger amounts of unlabeled data in WE languages. The tasks are focused particularly on linguistic aspects of speech, while nonlinguistic/paralinguistic aspects are not evaluated.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The tasks are focused particularly on linguistic aspects of speech, while nonlinguistic/paralinguistic aspects of speech relevant to e.g. speech synthesis or voice conversion are not evaluated. FLEURS is complete at more than 97%.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating cross-lingual speech representations, Training, Testing, Validation, Fine-tuning
